column7: 1.  How do you currently capture and record new sales leads? (e.g. notepad, spreadsheet, WhatsApp, CRM tool, email inbox?)
column8: 2.  What stages does a sales opportunity go through at your company — from the moment a lead shows interest to when they become a paying client?
column9: 3.  How do you record client interactions such as meetings, calls, site visits, or product demonstrations?
column10: 4.  What information do you track per client or opportunity? (company name, contact person, product interest, deal size, probability of closing, next action?)
column11: 5.  How do you currently follow up with clients who have gone quiet or not responded in a while? Is there a reminder or calendar system?
column12: 6.  How are individual and team sales targets set? Are they weekly, monthly, or quarterly? Who reviews them and how?
column13: 7.  How do you currently prepare a sales performance report? How long does it take and who requests it?
column14: 8.  How do you find out if a product a client is asking about is currently in stock or expected soon?
column15: 1.  What is the biggest single challenge in tracking your sales pipeline? Has a deal ever been lost because of a process gap?
column16: 2.  Do leads ever fall through the cracks — i.e. a client who showed interest but was never followed up with? How often and why?
column17: 3.  How much time per week does the sales team spend on manual reporting, updating spreadsheets, or compiling pipeline updates?
column18: 4.  Do you currently have a clear view of which products or service categories clients are most interested in? If not, how does this affect your approach?
column19: 5.  Is it always clear which sales representative owns which client or deal? Have there been conflicts or duplicated outreach?
column20: 6.  Have you missed important follow-up deadlines with clients? What caused the miss and what was the impact?
column21: 7.  Is it currently easy to send product brochures, pricing sheets, or promotional materials to a list of clients at once? What is the current process?
column22: 8.  What information do you wish you had about a client before going into a meeting or making a call?
column23: 1.  Would a visual CRM pipeline (New Lead → Contacted → Proposal Sent → Negotiation → Won / Lost) help you manage your pipeline better? What stages would you add or remove?
column24: 2.  How useful would automated follow-up reminders be? For example: PlacewareBot reminds you to follow up with a client last contacted 5 days ago. Would your team use this daily?
column25: 3.  Would a bulk messaging feature — allowing you to send a single SMS or email to 50, 100, or 500 clients at once — save time? What types of messages would you send most often?
column26: 4.  Should PlacewareBot automatically generate a weekly sales performance report and email it to your manager every Monday morning?
column27: 5.  How important is it to see a client's full purchase history (what they bought, when, how much, which sales rep handled it) directly in the CRM view?
column28: 6.  Would a deal probability score (e.g. 78% chance of closing based on client engagement) help you prioritise which opportunities to focus on?
column29: 7.  Should managers be able to see each sales rep's individual pipeline, conversion rate, and activity level in a real-time leaderboard? Are there any concerns about this?
column30: 8.  If you could ask PlacewareBot a question in plain language — e.g. Which clients have not ordered in 60 days? — would you use this daily?
